analysis.title: Credit Macro PT ETF TRS Commentary - 1 Nov 2026
key_insights: Week's tape: optimism around earnings faded after hyperscaler results raised questions about capital spending, returns on AI investment and valuations. The FOMC held rates steady and elevated energy prices kept inflation risk in focus. Flows rotated from mega-cap growth into value and small caps.
Equities finished lower. The NASDAQ fell 2% while the Russell 2000 gained 1.3% as investors rotated out of mega-cap growth names.
US credit was mixed because higher vol challenged tight spreads. IG cash held in early in the week, then spreads widened approaching month-end on risk-off sentiment.

IG primary: no companies priced on Friday, after MSFT and five other issuers sold about $37bn of new debt on Thursday. The desk says the backdrop stays supportive for issuance, but tighter spreads and rising funding needs make issuer selection more important.

FICC ETF flows were constructive despite risk-off price action. LQD took in $1.7bn of primary net inflows and HYG $500mm. Drivers cited are the rate rally, hedging ahead of larger issuance agendas, and credit investors treating spread widening as an entry point.

Rates rallied into the weekend as the Fed held and the tech-led sell-off lifted demand for safer assets. The 10y yield finished about 4.9%, below the prior week's close. Elevated oil and persistent inflation risk still complicate Fed cuts, leaving markets sensitive to upcoming inflation prints.

Desk bottom line: there is still a gap between AI capex investment and evidence of meaningful returns from hyperscalers. Investors are wary of mega-cap tech weakness and more selective in fixed-income positioning.

Trade idea: the desk's favorite basket hedge is short 500mm of an IG 30y ex-hyperscaler basket on swap (about 107bp, 115 CUSIPs), paired with buying 431mm of UST on swap. It follows Amanda Lynam's Thursday note on segmented weakness in AI-related credit and the question of which hedges suit portfolios.

Rationale for the hedge: generic IG spread excluding hyperscalers has not widened meaningfully and sits at the 12th percentile on a 20y lookback, one of the richest valuations in credit. If hyperscaler financing conditions deteriorate, the weakness could leak into broader IG cash and the ex-hyperscaler names should catch up on widening.
Hedge carry is negative. The 12m net theta is (10,432,348) dollars, or (16.9)bp, made up of (8,221,571) break-even carry and (2,210,777) expected rolldown.

PT channel had one of its most active weeks on record, driven by a resurgence in market volatility and month-end rebalancing. The desk cites 33.2bn in inquiry across 433 inquiries, while its WTD table totals 18.9b/14.3b. The report does not reconcile the two.
PT flows were for sale across the board, though only marginally. The rate rally kept ETF basis pinned at fair to rich, which let PT users trade two-way.
IG PT flows were 1.3:1 better for sale by dv01, spread evenly across the curve with a slightly larger share in the front end (0-3y IG clients sell 1.7:1). HY clients were also marginal net sellers.
HY selling concentrated in low-quality paper, with dispersion continuing between tight-trading BBs and single-B and CCC credits. By rating, CCC clients sell 1.7:1 and BB flows are balanced.
Tech on PTs stayed extremely balanced despite mega-cap tech driving the week's sell-off. The desk calls this surprising.

Sector skew: outsized client supply in basic materials (IG 2.0:1 sell, HY 1.6:1 sell) and financials (IG 1.6:1 sell, HY 1.5:1 sell). Clients bought industrials (HY 1.1:1 buy) and utilities (HY 1.2:1 buy) in HY.
earnings_insights: Hyperscaler earnings this week reignited questions over capital spending, returns on AI investment and stretched valuations, and reversed early-week optimism around earnings. The report gives no EPS or revenue figures.
MSFT and five other issuers sold about $37bn of new debt in the IG primary market on Thursday, following hyperscaler results.
